plants.name: Tulipa gesneriana
plants.description: A spring-flowering bulb with cup-shaped blooms on sturdy stems and broad, blue-green leaves. Thousands of cultivars exist, ranging from classic single cups to frilled parrot and double peony types. Late April is peak bloom in many temperate gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late spring (April to May in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Netherlands, northern Europe, and temperate regions of North America; originally native to Central Asia
plants.funFact: During the Dutch Golden Age in the 1630s, tulip bulbs became so valuable that a single rare bulb could cost more than a house in Amsterdam.

plants.name: Wisteria sinensis
plants.description: A vigorous woody twining vine that produces dramatic hanging clusters of fragrant flowers before its leaves fully emerge. It can climb pergolas, walls, and trees, and live for decades.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late spring (April to May)
plants.location: Native to China; widely cultivated in Japan, Europe, and the eastern and western United States
plants.funFact: Chinese wisteria twines counterclockwise, while Japanese wisteria twines clockwise, which helps distinguish the two species when not in bloom.

plants.name: Cercis canadensis
plants.description: A small deciduous tree whose clusters of pea-like flowers burst directly from bare branches and even the trunk before heart-shaped leaves appear. It is a valuable early nectar source for native bees.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to mid spring, lingering into late April in cooler areas
plants.location: Eastern and central North America, from Ontario to Mexico
plants.funFact: Redbud flowers are edible and have a mildly tart flavor; they are sometimes tossed into salads or used as a garnish.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A tall, fern-leaved tree covered with trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers in dense panicles. Flowering carpets streets and gardens with fallen blossoms. In the Southern Hemisphere, its main bloom is in spring (Oct-Nov), but in tropical and subtropical areas such as parts of Northern Hemisphere warm zones, flowering begins from late April into May and June.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Northern Hemisphere subtropics (late April to June); October to November in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to South America; grown in Florida, southern California, Mexico, South Africa, and Australia, with bloom starting in places like Mexico City around April
plants.funFact: Mexico City's jacarandas, introduced from Brazil in the early 1900s by a Japanese gardener named Tatsugoro Matsumoto, turn the city purple each spring.
